sentences.text:
Petitioners case is as Follows:
Petitioner no.1 and 2 are the parents of the deceased Muniraja.G.N.
3.

That on 21.05.2024 at about 00.05 AM., the deceased Muniraja was moving on a road as pedestrian in Hosakote- Chinthamani road, near SLV Nursery, wherein the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg No.KA-40-F- 1398 drove it, with high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the said Muniraja and caused the accident.
In the said accident Muniraju sustained grievousness injuries.

He was shifted to MVJ hospital, for first aid and later he was shifted to Akash Hospital wherein he took treatment as in patent for the accidental injuries and he died due to the accidental injuries on 23.05.2024.

Atopsy was conducted at Govt Hospital, Hosakote, later petitioners have performed the funeral and obsequies as per their customs at their native place and totally they have spent Rs.2,00,000/- for the same.

4. Petitioners alleged that prior to the accident deceased Muniraja.G.N was hale and healthy and he was 28 years old and he was working as coolie and he was 3 SCCH20 MVC No.4543/2024 earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
They further stated that, deceased is the main contributor for the income of the petitioners family.
Petitioners further stated that the alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligence act of the driver of KSRTC bus and the jurisdictional police have registered case in Cr.No.152/2024.
Petitioners alleged that the respondent is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners and they prays this tribunal to award the compensation amount with interest by allowing the petition.

5. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondent, respondent appeared through their/its counsel and filed their written statement by denying the entire version of the petitioners in toto.

Respondent specifically denied the age, income and profession of the deceased and contended that the deceased had died due to own negligent act and prays this court to dismiss the petition.
6.
In order to prove the case, petitioner No.2 examined herself as PW-1, produced and marked 16 documents which are at Ex.P.1 to 16 and she is fully cross examined.
Driver of the respondent examined himself as RW-1 and he is fully cross examined.
7. I have heard the arguments form the counsel appearing for both the sides and perused the entire records.

4 SCCH20 MVC No.4543/2024 The learned counsel appearing for respondent has relied on the following authorities;
1. 1994 ACJ 1303 - Hon'ble High court of Orrissa and cuttack.
2. ILR 1998 KAR 1934 3. MFA No.1749/2023 (MV-D) Hon'ble High court of Karnataka Narayanaswamy vs K.S.R.T.C on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129295388/

sentences.text:
On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following:
ISSUES 1.Whether the petitioners prove that on 21.05.2024 at about 00.05 AM., the deceased Muniraja was walking by the side of the road, near Bangahalli village, Chinthamani Road, Nandagudi Hobli, Hosakote Taluk, wherein the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg No.KA-40-F-1398 drove it, with high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the said Muniraja, due to which, he sustained grievous injuries and died due to the accidental injuries as alleged in the petition?
2.
Whether the respondent proves that Muniraja died due to his own negligent act?

3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
4. What order or award?

9. After carefully going through the evidence placed on record and taking into consideration of facts and 5 SCCH20 MVC No.4543/2024 attending circumstances of the case, my findings to the above issues are as follows;
 Issue no.1: In the Affirmative,
 Issue no.2: In the Negative,
 Issue no.3: In partly affirmative,
 Issue No.4: As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS  10. Issue No.1 to 3 :- I have taken these issues together for common discussion, so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW.1 being the petitioner no.2 and mother of the deceased Muniraja, she reiterated the petition averments in her examination-in-chief affidavit.
11.
According to the petitioners, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC bus that is Chowda Reddy S/o C.Pajjapaiah the (KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-40-F-1398).

Petitioners have tendered the police records that is FIR, complaint, mahazar,
sketch, IMV, Inquest, PM report, Final report, reply given by the KSRTC driver to the notice issued U/s 133 of M.V.Act which are at Ex.P1, 2, 4 to 7, 8 to 10 & 12.
12.

On careful perusal of the aforesaid documents it is evident that Chowda Reddy S/o C.Pajjapaiah was the driver of the offending bus and the jurisdictional police have filed final report against him after through investigation as per Ex.P.10.
Accordingly the said 6 SCCH20 MVC No.4543/2024 documents are the prima facie proof of the negligent act of the driver of the offending bus.

The Narayanaswamy vs K.S.R.T.C on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129295388/
3 aforesaid documents reveals that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of the driver of the KSRTC bus.

sentences.text: In the cross examination of PW-1, she clearly denied the suggestion that the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased.
She clearly deposed that the deceased was working as coolie and he was earning income of Rs.24,000/- per month.
Petitioner tendered medical bills/ receipts as per Ex.P.13.

The entry therein reveals that injured was admitted on 21.05.2024 and he took treatement for the accidental injuries as in patent and was died on 23.05.2024 and his family members have spent Rs.67,032/- towards medical expenses.
Ex . P.13
is not disputed nor denied by the respondent.
Nothing is elicited to establish the negligent act of the deceased as contended in his written statement.

13. In the cross examination of DW.1 he admitted that he was the driver of the offending bus as on the date of the incident and the jurisdictional police have registered the case against him and he has not challenged the final report filed against him.
It is true that the final report has attain the finality and respondent failed to probabilise the defence that the deceased died due to his negligent act.

14. Petitioners have not tendered the evidence to substantiate the nature of work and the income of the 7 SCCH20 MVC No.4543/2024 deceased accordingly the notional income of Rs.16,000/- has to be considered as the income of the deceased as the accident occurred in the year 2024.
15. Further more as per the entry in Aadhar card of the deceased which is Ex.P.16 the date of birth of the deceased is 16.01.1982.
Accordingly the age of the deceased as on the date of the accident was 42 years and multiplier 14 is applicable.

16. Deceased was self employee and he was bachelor, accordingly 25% should be added towards his monthly income for future prospectus and 50% should be deducted from his monthly income towards his personal expenses.
17.

The loss of dependency is calculated as follows:
1

Monthly income `.16,000/-
Add: 25% of income future prospectus `.4,000/-
`.20,000/-
2 Less; 50% for personal living expenses `.10,000/- 3

Monthly income `.10,000/-
4 Medical bills `.67,032/-
Rs.10,000 (income)X 12 (month) X 14 `.17,47,032/- (Multiplier ) Accordingly petitioners are entitled for Rs.17,47,032/- as compensation under the head Loss of Dependency.

Funeral Expenses, transportation etc., Accordingly as per the judgment in Praneya sethi case,
minimum amount of Rs.15,000/- can be awarded under this head.

20. Loss of Consortium :
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma G.I.C V/s Nanuram case, wherein the concept of consortium is categorically discussed.

In this petition, the petitioners are the wife,
children and mother of the deceased, accordingly they are entitled for consortium of Rs.40,000/- each.

Accordingly petitioners are entitled for Rs.40,000X2 =
Rs.80,000/- as compensation under this head.
21. Except the aforesaid compensation amount, petitioners are not entitled for compensation in any other heads.

22. In total the petitioners are entitled for compensation as follows;
Sl No. Compensation under the Head Amount 1 Loss of dependency `.17,47,032 /-
2 Loss of estate `.15,000/-
3
Funeral expenses & transportation `.15,000/- 4 Loss of Consortium `.80,000/-
In total petitioners are entitled for compensation amount of Rs.18,57,032/-.
9 SCCH20 MVC No.4543/2024 23. Rate of Interest:

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a.

As per the police records the accident took place due the sole rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle which belongs to Respondent.

In the present case, facts and attending circumstances and contention of the respondent is entirely different.

Accordingly I am answering issue no.1 in the affirmative, issue no.2 in the negative and issue no.3, in partly affirmative.

ORDER Petition

U/s 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 is partly allowed with cost.

Petitioners are entitled for compensation amount of Rs.18,57,032/-
with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition, till its realization.

Petitioners are entitled for 50% each, in the total compensation amount with interest.

After depositing the compensation amount with interest, petitioners are permitted to withdraw their entire share of compensation with interest through K2, after compliance of mandate of circular No.39/2020 dated 17.01.2020.
[ Advocate fee of Rs.1,000/- is fixed.
